title: Elastic cushion allocator and billing explainability
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Customers on Dedicated occasionally consume short-lived extra throughput during traffic spikes. Current surge handling grants temporary capacity from shared pools but billing and charge attribution are opaque to customers and to our support teams. This leads to high-severity billing disputes and operational load during post-incident reconciliations.

Goal: Implement an "elastic cushion" allocator (a lightweight transient headroom mechanism) that: (1) deterministically assigns temporary capacity to tenants during short spikes; (2) tracks per-tenant provisional credits and exact meter attribution; (3) exposes clear, queryable billing explanations in the Console and invoices. The feature must preserve SLOs for existing tenants, respect dedicated isolation guarantees, and provide controls for operators to reclaim provisional capacity when required.
acceptance_criteria: Elastic cushion allocator routes transient requests to tenant-local headroom where available and falls back to regulated shared pools with policy-based prioritization.
Per-tenant provisional credits are logged as line-items in usage events and visible in the Console (token-level and time-window aggregation).
Billing engine produces an explainability payload for any overage charge including: route policy id, cushion allocation id, time window, and reconciliation status.
Operators can run a reclaim action that converts provisional credits to permanent overage or refunds them according to policy, with an audit trail.
New metrics show cushion allocation rate, reclaim events, and the ratio of provisional-to-finalized charges; thresholds trigger alerting when abnormal patterns arise.
implementation_notes:
Design highlights:
- Allocator: lightweight state machine attached to each tenant's fleet controller. Maintains a small ring of cushion slots (configurable per-tenant) charged as provisional credits. Allocator input signals include short-window RPS/latency spikes, queue lag, and KV-cache miss rate.
- Policy layers: per-tenant policy (priority, max cushion size, refundable flag) + global policy (fairness factors, emergency cap).
- Metering: Emit a new usage event type `cushion_alloc` and `cushion_adjust` with the cushion_id (UUID), requested_tokens, granted_tokens, and provisional_amount_usd. These events flow into the billing ingestion pipeline with a `provisional` flag.
- Reconciliation: Background worker aggregates provisional events and either materializes them into permanent overage events or issues refunds. Worker uses a sliding 10–60 minute window configurable per-tenant.
- Console/UI: New 'Capacity Cushion' tab under Dedicated -> Billing that surfaces allocation timelines, per-cushion explainability, and an appeal button linking to support workflows.
- Operator controls: CLI commands and an internal admin page to view active cushions and force-reclaim by cushion_id.

Trade-offs & decisions:
- We prefer per-tenant tiny cushions over long-lived shared surge pools to reduce cross-tenant interference. This slightly increases per-tenant state but simplifies reconciliation.
- Provisional credits are preferred to immediate invoicing to avoid confusing customers during transient blips; however, we must keep reconciliation bounded to avoid long-lived uncertainty.
- To keep latency impact minimal, allocator decision logic runs in the fleet controller process and emits async events to billing; no blocking I/O on request path.

Open questions:
- Exact default cushion size per tier (suggested: 5% of committed throughput, capped at 500 RPS).
- Refund policy windows and SLA for reconciliation (30 min vs 4 hours).
- How to represent cushion usage on daily invoices vs monthly statements.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (alpha, internal): Enable elastic cushion for 10 internal tenants in staging. Watch allocation rates and reconciliation correctness.
Phase 2 (beta, opt-in): Expose opt-in toggle for selected enterprise customers with telemetry and billing explainability UI.
Phase 3 (gradual GA): Default-enable for Standard+ dedicated customers; provide tenant-level controls and a 7-day grace reconciliation window.
Safety measures: start with small default cushion (1-2%), global emergency cap, and an operator kill-switch that drains all cushions instantly.
Monitor: dedicated-cushion-alloc-rate, cushion-reconcile-latency, cushion-refund-rate, billing-dispute-count
comments: 2025-03-01 - Ava Martinez: Created ticket after customer postmortem with ACME Corp. They saw 45 minutes of unexplained overage during a short traffic surge. See incident notes: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-9983

2025-03-03 - Ravi Singh: Spike allocator prototype pushed to feature/elastic-cushion. Initial design uses per-tenant ring buffer + fairshare global arbiter. PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4872

2025-03-04 - Jordan Kim (SRE): Reviewed allocator prototype. Feedback: ensure allocator doesn't increase tail latency under CPU pressure; suggested offloading non-critical accounting to background worker. Marked 'needs perf benchmark'.

2025-03-06 - Priya Desai (Billing): Requested explicit schema for provisional events. Added fields: cushion_id, provisional_amount_usd, refund_status. Updated billing ingestion contract at: https://docs.redwood.ai/billing/provisional-events

2025-03-08 - Ravi Singh: Implemented provisional event emitter and reconciliation worker. Running end-to-end in staging with 10 tenants. Observed occasional double-counting bug during failover (working on fix).
2025-03-10 - Grace Li (Design): Mockups for Console 'Capacity Cushion' tab uploaded: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0BxyzUI/cushion-mockups
2025-03-11 - Ravi Singh: Fixed double-counting during failover by adding idempotency checks keyed by cushion_id + request_id. Reconciliation tests added. Loading internal alpha today.
2025-03-12 - PM review (Elliot Park): Reviewed alpha telemetry. Request: add 'appeal' CTA in UI linking to support flow and include per-cushion raw logs for 24 hours. Marked for beta release scope.
runbook: Internal runbook for cushion incidents: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/Cushion+Runbook. Key steps: 1) Identify cushion_id and tenant; 2) Assess reclaim eligibility; 3) Run `admin reclaim <cushion_id>` or trigger refund; 4) Notify customer if settlement > $1000.
